t.E552.agn: In 2018, EFSA saw no indication of genotoxicity or developmental toxicity for calcium and magnesium silicate and talc; however, noting that accumulation of silicon from calcium silicate in the kidney and liver of rats had been reported and that there were no reliable long-term toxicity, carcinogenicity and reproductive data, it concluded that their safety as additives could not be assessed. It stated that the group ADI set by the SCF in 1991 for silicon dioxide and silicates was no longer valid.
t.E552.eff.0.t: EFSA could not assess its safety because there are no reliable long-term toxicity, carcinogenicity and reproductive data
t.E552.found.0: Powdered foods, sliced or grated cheese, foods in tablet form and food supplements (E 551–553 group)
t.E552.found.2: Carrier in colour, emulsifier, polyol and nutrient preparations
t.E552.prod: It is a chemically produced silicate.
t.E552.regx.0: Re-evaluated; safety could not be assessed due to lack of data; the SCF group ADI was considered no longer valid.
t.E552.regx.1: Permitted at specified levels in powdered and tablet-form foods, cheese, salt, seasonings, chewing gum surfaces and food supplements (E 551–553 group).
t.E552.summary: Calcium silicate. It prevents caking in salt and powdered products.
t.E552.what: It is calcium silicate, which prevents caking of powdered foods.
